root_cause.text: Bluetooth socket destructors in HCI, ISO, L2CAP, and SCO failed to free SKBs queued in the socket’s sk_error_queue after TX timestamping support was added, so unread timestamp/error-queue packets leaked on socket teardown or controller removal.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “When TX timestamping is enabled via SO_TIMESTAMPING, SKBs may be queued into sk_error_queue and will stay there until consumed… these SKBs will leak,” and the patch fixes this by adding `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue);` to `hci_sock_destruct`, `iso_sock_destruct`, `l2cap_sock_destruct`, and `sco_sock_destruct`; it also cites the introducing change `134f4b39df7b ("Bluetooth: add support for skb TX SND/COMPLETION timestamping")`.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is that Bluetooth socket destructors did not free SKBs left in sk_error_queue, causing leaks on teardown. This group directly fixes that by purging the HCI, ISO, and L2CAP socket error queues during destruction.
The change directly matches the root cause: it purges the SCO socket sk_error_queue during destruction, freeing queued error SKBs that would otherwise leak on teardown.

candidates.rationale: The destructor purged receive and write queues but not sk_error_queue; this line shows teardown cleanup stopped without freeing queued timestamp/error SKBs, directly embodying the incomplete cleanup that caused the leak.

ISO socket destruction cleaned write queue but omitted sk_error_queue, leaving unread TX timestamp/error packets allocated. This statement marks the end of the incomplete purge sequence responsible for the leak.
L2CAP teardown purged standard queues only; failure to also purge sk_error_queue leaked queued SKBs. This statement is the clearest pre-fix line showing the incomplete destructor cleanup.
SCO socket destructor stopped after purging write queue and did not free sk_error_queue contents, causing teardown leaks of unread timestamp/error SKBs.

vuln_statements.explanation: In the HCI socket destructor, cleanup stopped after purging the write queue and did not purge sk->sk_error_queue. Because TX timestamping enqueued unread SKBs there, this incomplete teardown caused leaked SKBs on socket destruction or controller removal.

In the ISO socket destructor, this statement marks the end of queue cleanup before the missing sk->sk_error_queue purge. As a result, queued timestamp/error SKBs remained allocated and leaked during teardown.
In the L2CAP socket destructor, purging ended here without freeing sk->sk_error_queue. Since TX timestamping support could leave SKBs queued there, teardown leaked those unread packets.
In the SCO socket destructor, cleanup ended after the write queue purge and omitted sk->sk_error_queue. This omission left queued timestamp/error SKBs unfreed, causing the leak on socket teardown.

The receive path may take the socket right before h
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 709fca500067524381e28a5f481882930eebac88
Author: Nguyen Dinh Phi <phind.uet@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 8 03:04:24 2021 +0800

    Bluetooth: hci_sock: purge socket queues in the destruct() callback
    
    The receive path may take the socket right before hci_sock_release(),
    but it may enqueue the packets to the socket queues after the call to
    skb_queue_purge(), therefore the socket can be destroyed without clear
    its queues completely.
    
    Moving these skb_queue_purge()
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows both the old queue-purge location and the new destructor-based handling. The root cause is that purging in release is racy because packets may still be enqueued after `hci_sock_release()`. In this commit, `hci_sock_release()` no longer purges queues (`skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_receive_queue);` and `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_write_queue);` are removed), and a new destructor is added: `static void hci_sock_destruct(struct sock *sk) { skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_receive_queue); skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_write_queue); }`, with `sk->sk_destruct = hci_sock_destruct;` set at socket creation. This means the function body shown (`hci_sock_destruct`) does contain the queue-purge logic relevant to teardown, so the vulnerable condition of leaving queued SKBs unfreed at final destruction is addressed. The vulnerable construct existed before this commit in `hci_sock_release()`, but in this commit version the fix is already present via destructor-based purging. Therefore, for this commit version: has_bug=true because the snippet directly reflects the vulnerable area/logic being addressed, and is_fixed=true because the correct destructor handling is now present.
